Flexible itinerary

Oct 15 arrival + 10-day trip framework

David arrives late on October 15. The Oakridge trip starts from Richland on October 16. Use the riding itinerary as a priority queue, not a fixed reservation sheet: spend the first good-weather windows on high country and move lower-elevation / shuttle-friendly rides into damp days.

Route overview from the trip notes: baseline is roughly 6 hours / 350 miles. Exact route should follow weather, traffic and any riding detour.
Direct mission — Richland → Oakridge

Get to camp and protect the next morning for a marquee Oakridge ride.

Central Oregon route — Bend / Sisters

Useful if you want Sisters Coffee, a Bend stop, or the dry-side riding bailout on the way.

Mt. Hood / 44 Trails detour

Surveyor's Ridge / Dog River or Road 44 larch riding can turn the drive into a ride day if color and trail conditions line up.

McKenzie River corridor detour

McKenzie River Trail and the Hwy 126 / hot-springs / waterfall corridor remain optional pivots rather than fixed itinerary days.

Trip rule: Oakridge is still the main objective. Detours only earn a day if conditions are materially better or the stop is genuinely special.

From the trip notebook

What the trip should feel like

Late-October Oakridge: fall color, natural singletrack and cool-weather riding.
Wet West Cascades atmosphere can be a feature when the tread is still firm.
Rain-day wins: waterfalls, McKenzie Pass, Newberry and Smith Rock.
Hot-spring corridor: McCredie, Terwilliger, Bigelow, Belknap, Paulina and Umpqua.
Multiple approaches keep the trip flexible around weather and larch color.

These images are embedded directly from the supplied trip document so the page does not depend on third-party image hosting.

No-shuttle strategy

Riding Oakridge under your own power

Still very good. The trade is straightforward: less descending per hour, more forest-road climbing, and more freedom from shuttle minimums and late-season cancellations.

RideShuttle needed?Self-powered qualityUse
Moon Point loopNo10/10One of the best pedal-from-bottom options.
Middle ForkNo9.5/10Excellent XC / backcountry day.
Dead MountainNo9/10Very pedalable and repeatable.
Salmon CreekNo9/10Easy logistics and lower effort.
ATCAHelpful8.5/10Big day if fully self-powered.
AlpineHelpful8/10Doable, but worse climb-to-descent ratio.
HardestyHelpful7.5/10Long grind for the payoff.
LawlerHelpful7/10Much better as a shuttle.
Larison RockHelpful7/10Short descent for a lot of climbing.

What the climbing looks like

  • Forest-service-road grinding
  • Sustained 6–10% grades
  • Long climbs rather than punchy technical climbing
  • 2,500–4,500 ft days come easily
  • Often a large climb before the “real” descent starts

Where shuttle money matters most

  1. Lawler + Hardesty double
  2. Alpine
  3. ATCA — especially with late-October daylight
Suggested mix: roughly 4 self-powered days + 2–3 shuttle days. Carry a real MTB light on remote pedal days.

Optional fall-color detour

Larch rides — Mt. Hood / Road 44

The trip notes treat mid-to-late October as the planning window for Oregon's western larches. This is an opportunistic detour, not a fixed day: color, snow and current closures decide it.

#RideWhy goCharacter
1Surveyor's Ridge → Dog RiverBest mix of larches, Mt. Hood views and satisfying riding.Rocky / rolling ridge + substantial descent.
2Fifteenmile / Cedar CreekQuieter eastern 44 Trails larch country.~11 mi / ~2,100 ft; more demanding than mileage suggests.
3Gunsight Ridge / ButteRugged adventure, open ridges and big views.Strenuous; most weather-sensitive.
4Eightmile / Knebal SpringsMore larch forest without committing to Gunsight.Knebal base loop ~9.4 mi / ~1,700 ft; extend through Eightmile.
5Metolius Preserve / Lake CreekMellow golden-larch option near Camp Sherman.Gentle singletrack / old roads; good late-October possibility.
Best two-day concept: Surveyor's / Dog River first, then Fifteenmile or Gunsight depending on weather. Anthony Lakes is only an opportunistic choice because of its ~7,100-ft base elevation.
44 Trails map ↗Surveyor's Ridge route ↗44 Trails Association ↗
If larches are peaking and trails are open, Road 44 / Parkdale is the one detour worth stealing time from Oakridge for.

Late-October decision logic

Weather & bailout strategy

Sept. 29 trip-note snapshot: warmer signal / neutral precipitation signal. The notes estimated roughly a 65–75% chance of a good-to-very-good Oakridge trip with 6+ quality riding days, while keeping Bend as the primary escape hatch.
50–65°FReasonable town-afternoon planning range
30s–40sLikely overnight planning range
1–1.5 in.Cumulative wet-cycle threshold to start thinking Bend
4,500 ftSnow-level threshold to stop forcing high-country rides

This is the dated planning snapshot captured in the Word trip notes, not a live forecast. Recheck immediately before departure.

☀️

Dry / tacky

Use it now: Moon Point → ATCA → Alpine.

🌦️

Light rain

Stay Oakridge. Lawler, Hardesty, Dead, Larison.

🌧️

Sustained wet cycle

2–3 wet days or saturated soil: move east to Bend / Redmond.

❄️

Snow < 4,500'

Stop forcing high-country plans. Ride low or bail east.

Oakridge

Coffee

  • Mane Street — sit-down local coffee vibe.
  • Double Trouble — fast / early shuttle-day caffeine.
Food
  • 3 Legged Crane — core post-ride pub stop.

  • Rim Nam Thai — curry / noodles for a cold day.

Hood River

Coffee

Food

Coffee

Food

Non-riding wins

Noteworthy stops

Salt Creek + Diamond Creek Falls

Near-perfect Hwy 58 stop: quick viewpoint or 2–3 hour waterfall hike.

McKenzie Pass / Dee Wright

Volcanic landscape and Cascade views. Weather-sensitive in late October; verify OR 242 status.

Proxy Falls

Short scenic hike; combine with Dee Wright if McKenzie Pass remains open.

Sahalie + Koosah

Easy McKenzie River waterfalls; great on a partial rain day.

Newberry / Big Obsidian Flow

Best non-MTB Bend-area destination, but high enough for October snow.

Smith Rock

High-desert cliffs and Crooked River. Good sunset / half-day Bend bailout stop.

Tumalo Falls

Easy Bend-area waterfall add-on near west-side riding.

Office Covered Bridge

Westfir / Alpine logistics landmark. Quick photo stop, essentially zero trip cost.

High Desert Museum

The correct answer to a truly ugly Bend weather day.

Aufderheide Scenic Byway

Forest drive linking Westfir toward the McKenzie corridor; use when you have time, not as a destination.

Pilot Butte

Cheap, easy Bend sunset panorama; road access can be weather-dependent.

Excellent full weather-bail day: Oakridge → Terwilliger → Sahalie / Koosah → Proxy Falls → Dee Wright → Sisters Coffee → Bend. Proxy + Dee Wright only work if OR 242 remains open.
